messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — sustained increase in 429/503 from hosted-api starting ~2m ago. Auto-escalation to oncall. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/hosted-api/429-503-trends (root)
Alex S: oncall here. seeing 429 spike primarily on /v1/embeddings and /v1/generate. 503s mostly gateway timeouts to model pool-12
Alex S: quick grep of logs shows repeat errors: "InvalidQuotaExceeded" for tenant-3456 and an unusual traffic surge from 34.88.11.0/22
Maya T: @Alex S good find. tenant-3456 is heavy. can we apply a temporary QPS cap for that tenant? runbook suggests tenant shaping to 10 qps as first step
Pranav R: +1 to shaping. also suggest switching heavy routes to model-compact-1 (lower memory) as fallback. will trigger canary fallback if shaping doesn't drop 429s
Alex S: running shaping command now:

```
# apply tenant qps cap
POST https://api.redwood-internal/config/tenants/tenant-3456/limits
{
  "qps": 10,
  "ttl": 900  # 15m
}
```

Alex S: applied. confirmed via config service -> returned 200. policing should be at the edge within ~30s
SRE Runbook Bot: Runbook link: https://docs.redwood/internal/runbooks/traffic_shaping. Steps executed: tenant cap, monitor 429/5xx trend, prepare rollback.
Maya T: watching Grafana — 429 rate pre-shape ~1250/min across cluster. after cap starting to see drop in /v1/embeddings 429s at 60s mark
Jane O: taking 30m handoff to follow mitigation and coordinate pager overflow if any. @Maya T you still on for rollback if needed?
Maya T: I can stay. I'll also open a short-lived dashboard for tenant-level metrics: https://grafana.redwood/d/tenant/tenant-3456
Pranav R: triggered model fallback on route `/v1/generate` for heavy tenants: config update:

```
- route: "/v1/generate"
  fallback_model: model-compact-1
  fallback_threshold: 3xx latency or >5% 429
```

Applied, propagating.
Alex S: after shaping + fallback, 429s from tenant-3456 dropped from ~800/min to ~120/min in 3m. overall cluster 429s down ~70% from peak. 503s to pool-12 also reduced but still seeing intermittent timeouts
Maya T: 503s appear concentrated on pool-12 nodes with high memory pressure. ops infra team, can we cordon one node and drain to see if that stabilizes? @Infra
Jane O: paging infra separately. Meanwhile I've increased alert thresholds to avoid noisy paging, but keeping a critical alert for >20% 429 rate sustained 10m
Alex S: logs show retry storms from SDK clients. adding brief global retry-suppression header via edge config: `X-Client-Do-Not-Retry: true` for 60s window for impacted routes
Pranav R: noted. also added a short-lived cache for certain embedding prefixes to reduce downstream load: TTL 30s
SRE Runbook Bot: Mitigation checklist: tenant shaping ✅, model fallback ✅, edge retry-suppression ✅, node drain requested ✅. Continue to monitor for 15m and then begin controlled rollback.
Maya T: metrics update — 15m after action: cluster 429s at 160/min, 503s down 80% vs peak. tenant-3456 at 8 qps observed. Good signal.
Jane O: I'll start handoff notes to next oncall in #eng-oncall: mitigation steps, commands executed, links to dashboards and runbook. Postmortem required — include tenant traffic pattern and SDK retry behavior.
Alex S: saving commands we ran to incident notes. Also captured traces for a sample request that hit fallback -> model-compact-1 successfully.
Maya T: plan: keep tenant cap for 30 more minutes, monitor. if stable for 30m, gradually relax to 20 qps then fully remove. Ops to follow on node drain outcome.
Pranav R: follow-up items: add tenant-level alerting for sudden QPS jumps, consider auto-shaping policy for tenants >Xx baseline, add SDK guidance to avoid retry storms.
Incident Bot: Incident status update: mitigation in progress — reduced customer impact. Next update in 15m or on significant change. :white_check_mark:
Jane O: thanks all. I'll update the incident doc and notify support to proactively message affected customers if we see further degradation. :thumbsup:
